section_1.title: The Quest for the Root (Prerequisites & Intuition)
section_1.content: Briefly introduce root-finding: we want to solve f(x)=0. Visualize this as finding where a curve crosses the X-axis. Explain the intuition of Newton's method: 'If you don't know the root, start with a guess, draw a tangent line to the curve at that point, and move to where that tangent hits the X-axis.'
section_1.example: A hiker (the point) trying to find the base of a valley (the root) by always walking along the steepest downward slope.

section_2.title: The Newton Iteration Formula
section_2.content: Introduce the mathematical formula: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Explain this as a feedback loop. Use a graphical animation where a point jumps closer to the root with every step, demonstrating rapid convergence.
section_2.example: A robotic arm adjusting its position based on the sensor error slope until it perfectly grips a bolt.

section_3.title: When Convergence Breaks: The Basin of Attraction
section_3.content: Explain that Newton's method doesn't always go to the nearest root. Sometimes it enters a chaotic loop or jumps between roots. Define the 'Basin of Attraction': the set of initial guesses that lead to a specific root.
section_3.example: Three magnets placed on a table; a metal ball dropped at different spots is pulled to different magnets.

section_4.title: The Birth of the Newton Fractal
section_4.content: Extend to the complex plane. If we color every starting point based on which root it converges to, the boundaries become infinitely complex. Show a zoom-in animation of the boundary regions to reveal the self-similar fractal patterns.
section_4.example: A 'Digital Map' where the borders between different territories (roots) show intricate, repeating snowflake-like patterns regardless of how much you zoom in.

section_5.title: Summary and Philosophical Takeaway
section_5.content: Conclude that simple deterministic rules (Newton's formula) can generate extreme complexity (Fractals). Reiterate that mathematical beauty often emerges from the limits of iterative processes.
section_5.example: A tiny acorn (the formula) growing into a complex, infinite-looking oak tree (the fractal).
